record.paper_title: A single impurity in an ideal atomic Fermi gas: current understanding and some open problems
record.original_question: Explain why the Chevy ansatz, obtained by truncating the impurity wave-function expansion to a single particle-hole pair, remains extremely accurate even for large scattering length where strong particle-hole correlations might be expected. Determine whether the particle-hole-pair expansion has a hidden small parameter, identify when that expansion fails if it does fail, and quantify how the truncation error in observables such as the energy and quasiparticle residue depends on the truncation order, the mass ratio m/M, and the interaction parameter 1/k_F a.

evidence.quote: We raise a few unsolved problems: ... why is the polaron ansatz so good.
Why is the Chevy ansatz so good?

The Chevy ansatz seems to be extremely good even for large scattering length where we would expect strong particle-hole correlations, particularly for the energy and Z [28]. Why? Does the particle-hole pair expansion of the wave function have a hidden small parameter? And when does it fail (if ever)?
We would like to have a more quantitative control of the error when truncating the expansion at a certain order.

Are these two effects enough to show that terms with larger number of particle-hole pairs have smaller contributions and can we estimate the error in various quantities when truncating to a certain order in particle-hole pair number? Also, how would this error vary with m/M and 1/kFa?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single impurity of mass M immersed in a non-interacting three-dimensional Fermi sea of identical fermions of mass m at zero temperature, with Fermi momentum k_F. The impurity interacts with the bath fermions via a short-range two-body interaction characterized by the s-wave scattering length a, so that the dimensionless coupling is 1/(k_F a). Define the variational "particle-hole" expansion of the polaron ground state by writing

|Ψ_n⟩ = α_0 c^†_{p=0} |FS⟩ + Σ_{|k|>k_F, |q|<k_F} α_{k q} c^†_{q-k} a^†_k a_q |FS⟩ + (two particle-hole terms) + … + (n particle-hole terms),

where |FS⟩ is the filled Fermi sea, a^†, a are bath-fermion operators, c^† creates the impurity, and the coefficients are determined by minimizing ⟨Ψ_n|H|Ψ_n⟩/⟨Ψ_n|Ψ_n⟩. The case n=1 is the Chevy ansatz (one particle-hole pair).

Numerical evidence indicates that, even at unitarity 1/(k_F a)=0 and on the attractive side, the n=1 truncation reproduces the polaron energy E and quasiparticle residue Z to remarkable accuracy (within a fraction of a percent for E in the equal-mass case).

(a) Provide a rigorous explanation for why the n=1 (Chevy) truncation is so accurate over the entire range of 1/(k_F a), and identify a hidden small parameter (if any) controlling the convergence of the n-particle-hole expansion.

(b) Determine the regime, as a function of the mass ratio m/M and the interaction parameter 1/(k_F a), in which the particle-hole expansion fails to converge or converges only slowly.

(c) Establish quantitative bounds, scaling laws, or asymptotic estimates for the truncation error |E_n − E_∞| and |Z_n − Z_∞| as functions of the truncation order n, the mass ratio m/M, and 1/(k_F a).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has provided partial answers: extending the ansatz to higher particle-hole orders shows destructive interference between higher-order channels, accounting for the basic Chevy ansatz's percent-level accuracy at unitarity; quantitative improvements with two particle-hole excitations have been computed and connections to diagrammatic theory established (variational coefficients = on-shell vertex functions). However, no rigorous identification of a hidden small parameter, no proven error bounds in n, m/M, and 1/(k_F a), and no general criterion for failure of the expansion (e.g. near polaron–molecule transition or extreme mass ratios) has been established. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Exact theory of the finite-temperature spectral function of Fermi polarons with multiple particle-hole excitations
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative improvements at low temperatures with the inclusion of two-particle-hole excitations, in polaron energies and decay rates; variational coefficients identified with on-shell vertex functions.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-particle-hole extensions and equivalence to diagrammatic theory have been worked out, refining but not closing the question.

status_evidence.title: Polaron spectroscopy of interacting Fermi systems
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order particle-hole channels interfere destructively, explaining the remarkable precision of the basic Chevy ansatz at unitarity.
status_evidence.claim: Destructive interference among higher particle-hole channels offers a partial mechanism for accuracy of n=1 truncation.

status_evidence.title: Competing few-body correlations in ultracold Fermi polarons
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses regimes (mass ratio, coupling) where additional few-body correlations become important.
status_evidence.claim: Failure regimes are partially characterized for extreme mass ratios but no rigorous error bounds exist.
